name: Tyrosine supplements for tanning

lead: L-tyrosine is a common amino acid and a building block of melanin, and some tanning products and supplement sellers suggest taking it orally or applying it topically to boost tanning. The appearance payoff people want is a faster or deeper tan.

The chain is biochemical: melanocytes convert tyrosine into melanin after UV exposure, so proponents reason that extra tyrosine supplies more raw material. Tyrosine's role in melanin is established biology; published supplement research has focused on neurotransmitters and performance under stress, and no human studies have tested it for tanning or skin colour.

paras: People take it as a supplement or use lotions containing it, usually alongside sun or sunbed sessions, as tyrosine does not replace UV in the tanning process.
Tyrosine is sold as a dietary supplement. The tanning it is paired with involves UV exposure, which is classified as a carcinogen and causes sunburn and skin ageing.

web.title: Can L-tyrosine supplements make you tan? (New Beauty)

angle.text: You take tyrosine pills or apply lotions on the theory that more of melanin's building block means a faster or deeper tan. Tyrosine's role in melanin production is established biology. Human trials of it for tanning have not been published.

lead: Tyrosine supplements for tanning is the practice of taking L-tyrosine, a standard amino acid, as pills or applying it in lotions to help the skin darken or tan faster. The appeal is cosmetic: a deeper, more even tan from less sun, or a tan for people who say they tan slowly.[1][2] The idea rests on tyrosine's role as the starting material for melanin, the pigment made by melanocytes.[3][4]

Tyrosine is a conditionally essential amino acid that the body makes from phenylalanine and obtains from protein-rich foods; it is also sold as a dietary supplement and is a precursor of neurotransmitters such as dopamine.[3] Tanning involves increased melanin production after UV exposure.[4] Bodybuilding forums have long carried the suggestion: a 2008 T Nation thread advised a few grams of L-tyrosine for people who have trouble tanning, and a poster in a 2009 thread described adding it to a sun routine alongside melanotan.[2][5]

The idea resurfaced on social media, where dermatologists quoted by New Beauty described it as a TikTok claim without supporting evidence, noting that tanning depends on more than the amount of melanin precursor available.[1] Published research on supplemental tyrosine has concentrated on cognition and stress rather than pigmentation.[3]

paras: Tyrosine is one of the 20 standard amino acids and a precursor of melanin as well as of dopamine and norepinephrine.[3] Melanocytes make melanin, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation, and tanning is increased melanin production after UV exposure.[4] Dermatologist Stacy Chimento, quoted in New Beauty, explained that the body converts L-tyrosine to melanin via the enzyme tyrosinase.[1]

sections.h: Use in tanning and bodybuilding communities
paras: Supplement marketing points to the melanin pathway as a reason extra substrate could support more pigment.[1] In forum posts from 2008 and 2009, T Nation users recommended taking L-tyrosine before sun exposure, noting it was already an ingredient in some pre-workout products, and another poster listed it as a first step before getting sun alongside melanotan II and vitamin D.[2][5]

New Beauty reports that a study in Comprehensive Series in Photosciences found oral L-tyrosine did not induce tanning or enhance UVB-induced tanning, and that a Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology paper reported tyrosine pills had not been shown to work.[1] Dermatologists quoted there Jacquiline Habashy and Deborah Longwill said the claim lacks support and that tanning depends on several factors besides melanin production.[1]

No studies found of tyrosine as a tanning aid that this wiki could cite directly. The New Beauty article cites a study in which oral L-tyrosine did not induce tanning or enhance UVB-induced tanning.[1] Research on supplemental tyrosine in healthy people has otherwise examined cognition and mood under demanding conditions, with a 2015 systematic review concluding it may benefit working memory under stress.[3]

Supplemental tyrosine is widely sold as a dietary supplement.[3] New Beauty notes the FDA has not approved L-tyrosine for tanning, and Chimento notes that L-tyrosine can also be converted to compounds that may affect mood and stress responses.[1] Tanning itself requires UV exposure, whose health risks, including skin cancer, are documented separately.[4]

lore.intro: The tyrosine-for-tanning idea appears in bodybuilding forum threads as a tip for people who tan poorly.[2][5]

claims.claim: A few grams of L-tyrosine before sun exposure helps you tan.
